A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DMAD research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary materials support reliable comparison, including content moved between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: V1 reports original nuScenes experiments with DMAD, including perception, prediction, planning, decoder ablations, SHAP analysis, and supplementary sensitivity studies.

after.justification: V2 retains the original DMAD experiments and adds SparseDMAD comparisons, vectorized mapping results, and occupancy-prediction outcomes.

M1.justification: V2 adds a SparseDrive adaptation that explicitly removes front-camera features from ego-query construction (Section 4.1). The core parallel decoders, reference-point exchanges, finite-difference velocity estimation, and UniAD planning module remain unchanged.

E1.justification: NuScenes remains the sole dataset and driving domain. Table 3b extends evaluation from raster map segmentation to vectorized mapping of pedestrian crossings, lane dividers, and road boundaries. The newly reported occupancy scores concern a module described as retained, rather than establishing newly added training coverage.

E2.justification: SparseDrive becomes a second reproduced baseline across Tables 1–5, substantially extending the central comparisons. The new vectorized-mapping comparison includes MapTR and VAD. VPN and LSS disappear from the segmentation comparison, and PnPNet disappears from the prediction comparison, although LSS and PnPNet remain cited.

E3.justification: V2 introduces SparseDrive's four-frame configuration and vectorized-mapping AP/mAP evaluation, while retaining UniAD's three-frame control and two-stage scheme. The stage-two description changes from explicitly frozen BEV extraction to training all modules together; whether this reflects changed execution or rerunning retained experiments is unstated.

E4.justification: The standalone dense-intersection perception/prediction demonstration in v1 Section 4.5 and Figure 5 is removed. Decoder, queue-length, and prediction-horizon ablations remain unchanged, as do the four collision case studies. SHAP analysis is retained and relocated, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The SHAP bars represent feature contributions, and their rearrangement does not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive SparseDrive/SparseDMAD results, including stage-two NDS of 0.523/0.534, vector-map mAP of 0.549/0.587, and average collision rates of 0.097%/0.093%. Supplement Section 8 adds occupancy IoU: DMAD 62.7% near and 39.8% far, versus UniAD 62.9% and 39.6%. Matched existing UniAD/DMAD values and Tables 6–8 remain unchanged; removed comparator rows lose their results.

T1.justification: The Bayes-filter equation and decoder update equations retain their mathematical substance. Bayes-filter background moves into Supplement Section 7, and decoder equations use generalized sensor-embedding notation. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The divide-and-merge thesis remains, but v2 broadens its claimed applicability from UniAD to UniAD and SparseDrive. The conclusion extends negative-transfer elimination from object detection/tracking to object and map perception. The unchanged-planning-module claim is restricted to UniAD, and the abstract replaces specific percentage gains with broader performance claims.

C2.justification: Supplement Section 8 adds a substantive limitation: upstream improvements do not transfer to occupancy prediction, possibly because separated motion features lack spatial information. V2 also explains the different planning benefits for UniAD and SparseDrive and corrects the prediction discussion from reducing false positives to false negatives. Explicit open-loop criticisms and the proposed future closed-loop evaluation are removed.

D1.justification: V2 adds a DMAD code link and documents SparseDrive-specific settings, UniAD's random ego-query initialization, and the retained occupancy module's cross-attention. It removes the explicit Panoptic SegFormer map-decoding detail and the Table 1 statement identifying the source of VAD results.

R1.justification: V2 adds SparseDrive and positions DMAD across dense BEV and sparse scene representations. Panoptic SegFormer and Cross-view Semantic Segmentation references disappear. Most related-work coverage and the central positioning around separating semantic and motion learning remain intact.

P1.justification: V2 substantially edits the existing abstract, introduction, contributions, method exposition, and experimental narrative, including generalizing BEV-specific terminology to sensor embeddings. SHAP discussion moves into main Section 4.5, Bayes-filter background moves into the supplement, and the conclusion is rewritten.

P2.justification: The experimental presentation is substantially reorganized: Tables 1–5 expand or change structure, especially Table 3's separate segmentation and vectorized-mapping panels. The full-page supplementary SHAP figure becomes a compact six-panel main-text figure, replacing the standalone intersection visualization. Overview labels and several captions are also revised.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the previously UniAD-only validation with SparseDrive comparisons and vectorized-mapping evidence, adds a code link, and documents an informative occupancy limitation. These improve support for portability and clarify an applicability boundary. Broader across-task claims and reduced discussion of open-loop limitations weaken qualification, so the evidence supports a limited overall improvement.
